articles.title: Recording a faulty public streetlight without approaching electrical equipment
articles.summary: A clear location reference helps report lighting faults while avoiding electrical hazards.

sections.title: Record from a safe place
paragraphs: Identify the location by street name and a nearby landmark, or by a pole number only if it is already readable without approaching the equipment.
Note whether the lamp appears dark, flickering or damaged, and when this was observed. Avoid interpreting a single observation as evidence of the whole street's condition.

sections.title: Report and review
paragraphs: Use the relevant council, highway authority or lighting operator's published reporting channel; ownership may differ by road or site.
Never touch a damaged column, exposed wiring or fallen equipment. If there is an immediate danger, keep away and contact the appropriate emergency or infrastructure service.

articles.title: Reporting a blocked public road drain before heavy rain
articles.summary: Observation-based reporting helps distinguish a public drainage concern from a safe household task.

visual.alt: A three-item checklist for noting a drainage concern from a safe location, describing visible debris and reporting the location without entering the road or touching a drain.
visual.caption: A reporting prompt, not a drain-clearing procedure.

sections.title: Observe without intervening
paragraphs: From a safe public position, note the road or pavement location and whether visible leaves, litter or standing water appear near a drainage opening.
Do not enter traffic, move a cover, step into floodwater or attempt to clear a public drain. What looks blocked may have another cause.

sections.title: Send useful details
paragraphs: Provide the nearest address or junction, observation date and an objective description through the responsible highway or drainage authority's reporting route.
A report does not establish that the drain has been repaired. Recheck official information if access or flooding risk affects a journey.

articles.title: Distinguishing an expired weather warning from a superseded notice
articles.summary: A saved warning may have been replaced even before its original end time.

visual.alt: A three-step reading sequence comparing the issue time, stated validity period and latest authoritative source for a saved weather warning.
visual.caption: A saved warning is historical information, not a live alert.

sections.title: Read the notice accurately
paragraphs: Preserve the original issuing organisation, issue time, geographical area, warning type and stated valid period when saving a notice offline.
A notice can be amended, cancelled or replaced. The end of its stated period and the date you saved it are different facts.

sections.title: Avoid stale decisions
paragraphs: When connectivity is available, consult the issuing organisation for the latest notice affecting the exact area; do not assume an older screenshot remains authoritative.
If offline, clearly label the copy as last checked at a specific time and use existing household plans rather than inventing a current warning status.

articles.title: Preparing accessible alternatives when a public lift is unavailable
articles.summary: Lift disruptions can affect step-free travel even when the building remains open.

visual.alt: A checklist of three planning questions about confirmed step-free access, staff contact and a practical alternative venue or journey.
visual.caption: Confirm arrangements with the responsible operator; this is not an evacuation plan.

sections.title: Identify the specific access need
paragraphs: Record the exact station, entrance, platform or public-building lift involved. A lift described as out of service may not be the only route, but never assume an alternative is step-free.
Consider the complete journey from arrival to destination, including connecting transport, doors and toilets where these matter to the person travelling.

sections.title: Confirm a workable plan
paragraphs: Ask the operator or venue about current access, assistance arrangements and any authorised alternative before setting out where possible.
Do not treat a static offline diagram as a route map or ask anyone to use unsafe stairs or improvised lifting. Revisit the plan if the disruption changes.

articles.title: Keeping a factual reference log after non-emergency storm damage
articles.summary: A simple record separates observations, reporting and follow-up without implying a damage assessment.

visual.alt: A sequence showing safe observation, a factual record and follow-up with the responsible party; it does not show damage inspection techniques.
visual.caption: Keep evidence factual and avoid entering damaged areas.

sections.title: Record only what is safely visible
paragraphs: From a safe location, write down the date, affected area and visible changes. Photos may help when they can be taken without approaching unstable structures, downed lines or floodwater.
Do not infer structural safety from photographs or enter a damaged area to improve the record. If there is an immediate hazard, prioritise distance and appropriate emergency reporting.

sections.title: Separate reports and outcomes
paragraphs: Keep the contact route, reference number, date reported and any written response together. Distinguish an acknowledgement from a completed repair.
Store private addresses and insurance information securely rather than in public shared notes. Professional assessment and insurer requirements remain separate from this record.

articles.title: Checking school closure messages during severe weather
articles.summary: School messages can change quickly and require a plan that respects each child's arrangements.

visual.alt: A three-item checklist for checking a school's own message, confirming individual arrangements and checking for updates.
visual.caption: This is a communication checklist, not a live school-status feed.

sections.title: Check the source and scope
paragraphs: Identify the school or childcare provider, date of the message and whether it applies to the whole site, a year group, transport or an individual activity.
Forwarded messages and screenshots can lose context. A weather warning for the wider region does not itself confirm a school closure.

sections.title: Coordinate privately
paragraphs: Use the school's established communication route and agreed household contacts to clarify collection, attendance or remote-learning arrangements.
Do not publish children's locations or contact details in open groups. Keep the message marked as provisional if the school has not confirmed arrangements.

articles.title: Recognising a temporary bus route number or destination change
articles.summary: Similar route numbers and destination displays can make disruption notices difficult to interpret.

visual.alt: A checklist comparing a bus route number, displayed destination and current operator notice before travel.
visual.caption: Offline prompts cannot confirm which bus is running now.

sections.title: Separate route identity from destination
paragraphs: Record the operator, usual route number, direction of travel and intended stop. A temporary number or shortened destination display does not necessarily mean the entire route has changed.
Read the date and affected journeys on an operator notice; school-day, evening and weekend services may be described separately.

sections.title: Confirm the boarding decision
paragraphs: Where possible, verify the current stop and destination through the operator or staff rather than relying only on a previously saved timetable.
For accessibility needs, confirm boarding arrangements and onward connections. Retain a clear offline note but do not present it as live vehicle tracking.

articles.title: Assessing the credibility of a temporary community support notice
articles.summary: A notice advertising help during disruption should be checked without sharing sensitive household details.

visual.alt: A three-question checklist for checking the named issuer, the specific offer and an independent verification method before relying on a community support notice.
visual.caption: Do not assume a printed or forwarded notice is officially endorsed.

sections.title: Check provenance and scope
paragraphs: Look for a named organiser, date, intended location, opening conditions and a way to verify the announcement independently. A logo or forwarded social post alone does not prove authenticity.
Distinguish voluntary community help from official services. An offline copy cannot show whether the offer is still operating or has capacity.

sections.title: Protect privacy and expectations
paragraphs: Before travelling or sharing information, check the organiser's legitimate contact route when connectivity allows and clarify any accessibility or eligibility arrangements.
Avoid sending identification, payment details or household absence information to an unverified contact. Record only the minimum information needed for a practical enquiry.
